I'm 64 this year, and my back reminds me of it every morning. Forty-five years on this land, and it's just me and my wife now — the children are working in Shijiazhuang and only come back for the big harvests. With only two pairs of hands, I have to be careful with labor. My 13.5 mu is split into two parts: 4.5 mu for cotton and 9 mu for wheat-maize rotation. I keep the cotton because Jimian 668 grows well here and the price has been decent, but I won't plant more than 4.5 mu because picking is back-breaking work at my age, and hiring pickers costs too much. The wheat-maize double crop is my insurance — the machines handle most of it, and I know it like the back of my hand.

For wheat, I sow in early October after running the rotary tiller over the maize stubble. I'm using an improved variety — Luyuan 502 has done well for me. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu, and I expect around 400 kg per mu again if the winter isn't too dry. For fertilizer, I spread 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing — that's about 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium per mu — and then I topdress with 30 jin of urea at jointing, which gives me roughly 14 kg of nitrogen per mu in total. The extension fellow says 15 kg nitrogen is enough, but I've always done a bit more to be safe; losing yield hurts more than wasting a few yuan on fertilizer. I'll irrigate three times: winter irrigation to protect against frost, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. Water from the well isn't free anymore with the meters, so three times is my limit. I'll spray pesticides three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice. I skipped herbicide two years ago and the weeds taught me a lesson.

For summer maize, the window after wheat harvest is brutally tight — sometimes only five or six days. I'll no-till plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed right behind the combine; this hybrid has done well for my neighbors and doesn't lodge easily. I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing — that's about 10 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I won't topdress because by July I'm busy with the cotton spraying. I'll irrigate twice if the summer drought hits, especially at the big trumpet stage. Three pesticide applications: one herbicide and two insecticide rounds for armyworm.

For cotton, I rotary till in mid-April and plant Jimian 668. Cotton is demanding but pays better per mu than grain. I use 100 jin of cotton compound fertilizer per mu as base — about 9 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 9 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs that potassium during flowering. I'll irrigate twice: once at flowering and once at boll-setting. The biggest headache is pesticides — I'll spray 14 times through the season, mostly insecticide for aphids and spider mites, plus one herbicide spray. I also use plant growth regulator four times to keep the plants from growing too tall. Last year I harvested about 600 jin per mu, so I'm hoping for 300 kg per mu again.

At my age, I don't take big risks. I do what worked last year, I watch what my neighbors do, and I don't try to save money on fertilizer only to lose yield. Cotton gives me cash, wheat-maize gives me stability. That's how I'll manage this year.
